PGS005217 is the best-supported direct match despite the target being phrased as “peripheral vascular disease”: it targets the closely aligned clinical endpoint “incident peripheral artery disease,” is disease-focused (not a UKB portability framework), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant coverage (~1.3M), and—critically—reports a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.66) plus a basic-covariate time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.731 with age/sex/PCs), with broad multi-ancestry evaluation. In contrast, PGS002055 and PGS001843 are from the UKB “Portability of 245 polygenic scores” framework and only show very small partial correlations (0.0175 and 0.0151), suggesting weak PRS signal in that setting; between them, the LDpred2 score (PGS002055) is structurally stronger than the very sparse penalized-regression score (PGS001843). PGS005158 is endpoint-restricted (PAD in type 2 diabetes) and extremely sparse (19 SNPs) with a weak HR (1.13), plus heavy clinical covariate packaging, making it least likely to generalize as a standalone PRS for the broader target trait.

PGS002040 is the strongest overall package for the target concept: it matches the trait EFO, uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with very large variant coverage, and has a directly PRS-comparable reported metric (partial-r=0.0276 in EUR) that is modest but coherent. It also edges its near-clone sibling PGS001833 from the same publication/endpoint/covariate context on the only comparable performance signal (higher partial-r), making it the best-supported pick within that family.

PGS001833 is the closest runner-up: same endpoint and evaluation context as PGS002040 but weaker partial-r (0.0218), and a smaller (though still non-sparse) variant set.

PGS001137 and PGS000990 come from the sparse snpnet “813 traits” UKB framework, which is systematically less reliable for external transfer than the portability-family genome-wide scores when endpoint fidelity is otherwise similar. Between those two, PGS001137 is preferred because it is a direct retinal detachment endpoint (not time-to-event/broader breaks) and shows stronger PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUC 0.573 vs 0.542; PGS-only R2 0.0066 vs 0.0021), both remaining plausible under the heritability ceiling sanity check.

Top pick favors the disease-focused multi-cohort thyroid-carcinoma PRS family with strong per-SD effect size evidence and broad multi-ancestry evaluation context, rather than relying on potentially covariate-inflated full-model AUROC alone. Among the near-clone 2026 multi-ancestry PRS-CS siblings, PGS005259 has the strongest within-family signals (higher full-model AUROC and higher OR/β than PGS005260 with essentially identical endpoint/validation context), making it the most plausible hidden-benchmark #1. PGS005260 is the closest runner-up as the same PRS-CS design with slightly weaker reported discrimination/effect size. PGS000208 shows a higher reported AUROC but it is also a full-model metric with explicit family-history covariate inclusion (comparability/leakage risk) and is EUR-only, reducing confidence that it will beat the newer multi-cohort disease-focused score externally. PGS000797 is a pan-cancer integration/derived-score context with time-to-event incident endpoint and additional covariates (BMI etc.), making its reported metrics less directly comparable for standalone PRS performance. PGS005258 (P+T, 84 variants) has an implausibly weak OR/β relative to its AUROC and is structurally much sparser than the PRS-CS siblings, so it is least likely to top an external benchmark.

PGS000135 is the strongest direct-match, endpoint-faithful schizophrenia PRS in the shortlist: phenotyping_reported matches schizophrenia, evaluation is EUR like the others in its publication family, covariates are basic (age/sex/PCs/platform/batch), and it has the best reported discrimination within the near-clone set (full-model AUROC 0.74 vs ~0.60–0.64 for siblings), with similarly genome-wide PRS-CS construction and high variant count. PGS000136 is the next best sibling with higher AUROC than the remaining PRS-CS options and a strong per-SD OR (~1.7). PGS000133 and PGS000134 are weaker siblings with lower AUROC and/or smaller OR. PGS002785 is deprioritized despite being labeled schizophrenia because its phenotyping_reported is cognitive function (explicit endpoint mismatch) and the reported partial R² is small and not directly comparable to schizophrenia case-control prediction.

All candidates are direct phenotype matches (squamous cell carcinoma; EUR evaluation), and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R2, so ranking leans on within-context performance/effect-size signals and comparability. PGS000461 is the strongest-supported among the PRSweb siblings: it has the highest full-model AUROC in that family (0.599 vs 0.593/0.589), the highest per-SD OR (1.491, meeting the ~1.5 strong-signal heuristic), and the highest pseudo-R² (0.0304) with only basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), making it the best bet for external benchmark performance. PGS000731 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.605) and a very tight OR estimate (1.44) with much larger evaluation N, but covariates are unknown and the study context differs (23andMe/RiskPipe), so its apparent edge is less interpretable/comparable than the clean PRSweb setup. Among the remaining PRSweb scores, PGS000463 edges PGS000465/PGS000120 on AUROC and similar covariates; PGS000465 has a higher top-1% OR but weaker per-SD OR/AUROC and lower pseudo-R²; PGS000120 is older, has weaker AUROC/OR, and offers no compensating PRS-comparable metrics.

PGS001280 is the strongest direct-match for pulmonary embolism with coherent endpoint fidelity (PE time-to-event but still PE-specific), clean/basic covariates, and the best PRS-comparable metrics among the EUR-evaluated snpnet siblings (highest PGS-only AUROC 0.60765 with similar PGS-only R2 0.01403, both plausible under the heritability ceiling). PGS001277 is a close runner-up with slightly higher PGS-only AUROC/R2 (0.61144/0.01508) but its endpoint is explicitly composite (PE +/- DVT), making it a less direct match than PE-only. PGS001279 and PGS001278 are broader/less PE-specific self-report composites and show weaker PGS-only AUROC, so they are less likely to top an external PE benchmark despite larger validation N for PGS001279. PGS003861 is PE-specific but is EAS-only with missing PRS-only metrics (only a full-model AUROC reported with unknown covariates), making its apparent performance non-comparable and less likely to win a general external benchmark.

All candidates are direct matches (bladder cancer / urinary bladder carcinoma) in EUR, and none reports clean PRS-only AUC/R², so we lean on endpoint fidelity + study archetype + within-family performance/effect-size tie-breaks. PGS000723 has the strongest overall external-validation posture: incident bladder cancer endpoint, evaluated in a very large multi-cohort setting (n≈400k) with minimal covariate adjustment (genotyping array only), and it shows the highest reported AUROC among the set (0.583 vs ~0.567–0.572), making it the most plausible hidden-benchmark #1 despite missing training N/effect sizes. Among the PRSweb siblings, PGS000613 (P+T, 15 variants) edges PGS000611 (GWAS hits) with slightly higher AUROC (0.571 vs 0.567), higher pseudo-R² (0.0125 vs 0.0114), and stronger OR signals (per-SD OR 1.301 vs 1.284; top 1% OR 2.91 vs 2.66) under identical covariates and validation context, so it ranks next. The MGI-based near-clones PGS000610 and PGS000612 are effectively indistinguishable (same metrics/effect sizes/variants), so they are placed last with no meaningful separation.

All three candidates are direct endpoint matches (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), from the same publication family, with identical EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry and the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), so the most reliable differentiators are within-family empirical performance/effect-size signals rather than method labels or variant count. PGS000471 shows the strongest validation evidence across multiple comparable fields: highest full-model AUROC (0.569 vs 0.557 vs 0.524), highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0255 vs 0.0154 vs 0.00141), strongest per-SD OR (1.401 vs 1.308 vs 1.09), and strongest top-1% vs rest OR (3.77 vs 2.45 vs 1.48). With no PGS-only AUC/R² reported for any candidate, these consistent within-context advantages make PGS000471 the best-supported likely external-benchmark performer. PGS000470 is the clear runner-up with intermediate effect sizes/metrics. PGS000469 underperforms markedly on AUROC, pseudo-R², and ORs despite being genome-wide, suggesting weaker realized signal in this setting.

PGS004162 is the most likely hidden-benchmark #1 because it has clean endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported=T1D), explicitly no covariates (covariates=0, reducing covariate-driven inflation risk), and provides both discrimination (AUROC≈0.77) and effect-size evidence (OR per SD≈2.89) in a direct disease evaluation setting. PGS004874 is a close runner-up with similarly clean covariates (PCs only) and very large evaluation, but it is incident/time-to-event framed and reports a comparable C-index (~0.77) with a slightly weaker per-SD effect (HR≈2.37), making it marginally less aligned to generic case-control benchmarking. PGS001297 has explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC≈0.77; PGS R2≈0.091, below the h2_liability ceiling) but comes from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework (snpnet across many traits), which is a consistent external-transfer penalty versus disease-focused direct-match scores. PGS000024 and PGS000021 show very high full-model AUROC (0.92–0.96) but lack comparable PRS-only metrics and include unknown/heavy clinical covariates (e.g., autoantibodies, BMI, age at diagnosis) or interaction modeling, so their reported AUROC is likely not PRS-comparable and is discounted for hidden benchmark performance.

PGS001536 is the best-supported direct match because its phenotyping is explicitly vitiligo (albeit time-to-event), it reports clean PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64193 and PGS-only R2=0.01621) with only basic covariates, and it has a coherent EUR development/evaluation context with additional multi-ancestry evaluation suggesting some robustness. The PRS-only R2 is well below the EUR vitiligo heritability ceiling (h2_obs~0.17), making it plausible and comparable.

PGS000738 has the right disease label (vitiligo) and EUR evaluation, but its endpoint fidelity is undermined by a clearly inconsistent phenotyping field (“Red hair”), and it lacks PRS-only metrics (only pseudo R2/full-model style reporting plus a beta), increasing risk of metadata contamination and reducing comparability.

PGS000760 is least suitable as a direct-match vitiligo risk score because its phenotyping is treatment/setting-specific (anti–PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients), making endpoint mismatch and transportability risk high despite a moderate HR (1.41) and large nominal training size.

PGS001306 is the best-supported direct-match because it has clean, explicitly PRS-comparable performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.630 and PGS-only R²=0.0204) under basic covariates, with a full-model AUROC (0.662) that is consistent with modest incremental lift—making it more interpretable for external benchmarking than candidates that only report full-model AUROC or partial-r. PGS001307 is similar but is a time-to-event endpoint (less direct for generic UC status) and shows weaker/less coherent full-model vs PGS-only metrics, so it ranks just behind. PGS004253 is disease-focused and uses a strong genome-wide shrinkage method with a strong OR (1.84 per SD), but its only AUROC is full-model (0.66) and the training ancestry is MAE with EUR-only evaluation, reducing comparability/transfer confidence versus the UKB-derived PRS-only metrics in PGS001306. PGS001855 provides only partial correlation (no AUROC/R²) from a portability framework context, making expected benchmark performance less certain. PGS002066 has weak reported discrimination (AUROC=0.57) and a near-null OR (1.11, CI includes 1), making it the least likely to rank #1 externally.

PGS002075 is the strongest direct-match on endpoint (urinary calculus/urolithiasis) with a method/structure (LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage; 731k variants) that typically transfers better than sparse models, and it has a slightly stronger PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0385) than its near-clone sibling PGS001864 (partial-r 0.0323) under the same portability-study context, covariates, and validation setting—making it the best-supported #1 candidate within that matched pair. PGS001864 is the clear runner-up as the same endpoint/publication/validation design but with weaker partial-r and a much sparser model (5.6k variants). PGS004563 and PGS004493 have good phenotype alignment (ICD N20 calculus of kidney and ureter; within the urolithiasis spectrum) and very large genome-wide variant sets, but they lack PRS-comparable discrimination metrics and have unknown covariates; between them, PGS004563 is preferred due to the stronger reported per-SD OR (1.283 vs 1.227) in the same study family/endpoint. PGS001250 is penalized most because it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (813 traits) and uses a time-to-event endpoint; despite having explicit AUC/R2 fields, its PRS-only AUC (~0.567) and R2 (~0.006) are modest and are less reliable indicators of top external-benchmark performance than the better-aligned, genome-wide shrinkage portability score.

PGS002308 is the strongest overall package for likely external-benchmark performance: it is a disease-focused, direct T2D score using PRS-CSx (cross-ancestry shrinkage) with very large genome-wide variant coverage and explicitly diverse evaluation ancestry, plus a strong per-SD OR (~1.96) that is a more PRS-informative signal than covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. PGS001781 is a solid runner-up (PRS-CS, genome-wide, incident T2D endpoint) with good reported discrimination, but its reported AUROC is full-model and its per-SD OR (1.52) suggests weaker standalone PRS signal than PGS002308. PGS000804/PGS000805 are near-clone GWAS-hit (582 SNP) scores from a disease-focused multi-cohort study with very large validation; however their headline AUROC is also full-model and includes BMI (making it less PRS-comparable), and the sparse SNP set is structurally less likely to win against genome-wide shrinkage in an external benchmark; between them, PGS000805 is marginally favored by essentially identical metrics and broader record support. PGS003103 is penalized as an ExPRSweb framework-derived score with weaker reported discrimination and smaller validation, making it least likely to rank #1 externally despite being a direct trait match.

Top pick: PGS005219. It is a direct obstructive sleep apnea endpoint (dominant clinical form of sleep apnea), built in a disease-focused multi-cohort setting (FinnGen + MGBB + MVP) with a genome-wide PRS-CS-style construction and very large variant count (~983k), which is structurally favorable for external performance. Although only full-model AUROC is reported (0.79, not PRS-only), it also reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR=1.98), which is supportive of genuine PRS signal and helps differentiate it from near-clones.

Runner-up: PGS005220 is essentially the same study/method/endpoint family and similarly high full-model AUROC (0.79), but its reported OR is materially weaker (1.53 vs 1.98), making it less likely to be the best external performer among the siblings.

Next: PGS003858 and PGS003857 are disease-focused MVP scores but are GWAS-hits-only (6 and 18 variants), which is typically less competitive than genome-wide shrinkage for a polygenic disease; their reported betas are small and they rely on full-model AUROC (0.77) that is not PRS-only. Between them, PGS003858 has the stronger beta signal (0.066 vs 0.014), so it ranks above PGS003857.

Last: PGS003213 is a pan-trait/framework-style ExPRSweb score with much weaker discrimination evidence (full-model AUROC ~0.53) despite genome-wide PRS-CS, making it least likely to win an external benchmark against the disease-focused OSA-specific models.

PGS000541 and PGS000542 are the cleanest direct uterine-cancer endpoint matches (same phenotyping_reported, same EUR-only UKB context, basic covariates only) and have comparable evaluation; between these near-clones, PGS000541 has slightly stronger and more consistent discrimination/effect-size evidence (higher AUROC 0.576 vs 0.572; slightly higher per-SD OR 1.311 vs 1.302; slightly higher Nagelkerke R²), so it is the best-supported pick. PGS001795 uses a methodologically strong genome-wide shrinkage approach and reports a PRS-comparable R², but it comes from a global-biobank framework-style analysis with a different mapped trait (uterine carcinoma) and its PRS-only R² is very small, making it a less reliable #1 than the coherent Cancer PRSweb uterine-cancer pair. PGS000075 has a high full-model AUROC but it is clearly covariate-heavy (many reproductive/hormonal factors and family history), so the AUROC is not comparable as PRS evidence; it is also endometrial (dominant subtype) rather than the umbrella label. PGS003740 has sparse metadata/performance (no AUC/R², unknown covariates) and very small training/validation, so it is least supported for external benchmark performance.

PGS001792 is the best-supported direct-match because it combines strong endpoint fidelity (primary open-angle glaucoma), a PRS-comparable metric (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out = 0.0321, plausibly below the liability h2 ceiling), and large-scale European validation with standard demographic/PC covariates; among the near-clone Global Biobank PRS-CS-auto scores, it also shows higher AUROC (0.777 vs 0.749) and slightly higher PRS-only R2 than PGS001797, making it the most plausible hidden-benchmark #1. PGS001797 is the closest runner-up but is weakened by much smaller validation (n=7,128) and lower AUROC/R2 in the same study family. PGS004944 has a strong reported OR (1.74) and huge validation size, but its only AUROC is a full-model value (0.748) and the phenotype is explicitly self-reported, making its performance evidence less PRS-clean/comparable. PGS002761 has a decent OR (1.68) but lacks comparable discrimination metrics and is a broader glaucoma endpoint, leaving less direct evidence for benchmark ranking. PGS000137 reports high full-model AUROC (0.8) but includes family history in covariates (inflation/leakage risk) and is an older sparse C+T score with small validation, so it is least likely to top an external PRS benchmark.
